**Test image observations:**
- A single mango leaf, mostly green and healthy-looking
- Small round/blister-like spots scattered across the leaf surface — these appear as small raised or indented circular marks
- The spots look like small galls or exit holes — round, scattered, some reddish-brown
- The leaf is not blackened, not powdery, not curled or crumpled

**Analysis:**
- The small round spots scattered across the leaf surface strongly resemble **Gall Midge** galls — round, blister-shaped, approximately 2-3mm, visible on leaf surface
- Not Sooty Mould (no black coating)
- Not Powdery Mildew (no white powdery growth)
- Not Cutting Weevil (leaf is not curled/crumpled/stripped)
- Not Bacterial Canker (no angular raised spots with halos)
- Not Anthracnose (no dark sunken lesions)
- Not Die Back (no twig withering/gum)

The round blister-like dots scattered across the leaf are characteristic of Gall Midge galls.
